argument_summary: The supportable position is narrower than full present-tense compliance. On the admissible record, certification is defendable only as caveated certification through the current audit packet itself: the packet must state the current aggregate result, state the environmental permit screening regression, and include explicit limitation language for that named use case. That reading does not rely on prior approval or informal monitoring as substitutes; it treats them only as context. The aggregate readiness evidence and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support release-level readiness, while the subgroup regression requires disclosure rather than denial.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is needed to support this position. The argument is policy-based and risk-weighted from the admissible evidence, not from launch-pressure considerations.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy does not allow prior approval or informal monitoring to satisfy current-release requirements, and I do not claim otherwise. The policy path that remains available is current-release documentation that reflects the current evaluation results and expressly discloses the material weakness for the named use case, unless there is approved mitigation or risk acceptance. Because no approved mitigation or risk acceptance is in evidence, the only defensible certification theory on this record is caveated compliance through explicit current-release disclosure in the certification packet.
concessions: The current record does not show approved mitigation or approved risk acceptance for the environmental permit screening weakness.
The current subgroup regression is real and must be described as a current limitation, not minimized by aggregate performance.
Prior approval of the same model family is contextual only because this release includes a changed retrieval configuration and a new evaluation batch.
Informal post-launch monitoring comments are not equivalent to reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language.
